title: Indian National Convicted of Voting Illegally in 2024 US Presidential Election
excerpt: A federal jury in Fort Worth convicted Khalwinder Singh Bhengura, a green card holder from India, of voting by an alien and falsely claiming US citizenship to register. Sentencing is set for February 11, 2027.
body:
• A federal jury convicted Indian national Khalwinder Singh Bhengura on October 27 of voting by an alien in a federal election and making a false claim of US citizenship to register to vote.
  • Bhengura became a lawful permanent resident on June 29, 2022, never applied for citizenship, and voted in person in Arlington, Texas, on November 5, 2024.
  • He faces up to five years in prison on the false-claim count and up to one year on the voting count, plus fines of up to $350,000 combined — and possible removal from the US afterwards.
  • Sentencing is set for February 11, 2027. Green card holders cannot vote in federal elections; only US citizens can.

A federal jury has convicted an Indian national of voting illegally in the 2024 US presidential election, the US Attorney's Office for the Northern District of Texas announced. Khalwinder Singh Bhengura was found guilty of voting by an alien in a federal election and making a false claim of US citizenship to register to vote.

After a two-day trial before US District Judge Mark T. Pittman, the jury deliberated for several hours and returned its verdict on October 27.

"Voting in our national elections is reserved for US citizens. Every unlawful vote undermines the voices of eligible citizens, and this office will hold accountable anyone who undermines our elections."

— Ryan Raybould, US Attorney for the Northern District of Texas

How the case unfolded

According to evidence presented at trial, Bhengura, a citizen of India, became a lawful permanent resident of the United States on June 29, 2022. He is not a US citizen and has never applied for citizenship. On August 1, 2024, he applied for a Texas driver license in Tarrant County and, in that application, checked boxes stating that he was a US citizen and wished to register to vote. Based on that application, he was registered to vote in Texas.

https://x.com/JewelsJonesLive/status/2115536512179736703

On November 5, 2024, Bhengura voted in person at the East Library and Recreation Center in Arlington, Texas, in a general election that included races for President, Vice President, US Senate and US House of Representatives.

What he faces

Sentencing is set for February 11, 2027. Bhengura faces up to five years in federal prison and a fine of up to $250,000 for the false claim of citizenship to register to vote, and up to one year in prison and a maximum fine of $100,000 for voting by an alien in a federal election. He could also be subject to immigration penalties, including removal from the United States after serving any prison term.

The case was investigated by the HSI Dallas field office, with assistance from the Election Integrity Unit of the Texas Attorney General's office and the Tarrant County District Attorney's Office, and prosecuted by Assistant US Attorneys Matthew Capoccia and Colin Duffy.

Part of a wider enforcement push

The conviction lands amid a nationwide series of election-related cases. The Department of Homeland Security said this week that dozens of non-citizens have been arrested in a voter fraud crackdown, including another Indian national arrested in Minnesota in September for allegedly making a false claim of citizenship to vote in the 2024 election. For the large population of Indian green card holders still years from naturalization, the practical rule is unforgiving: permanent residence confers the right to live and work in the US, but the ballot — and even a voter registration obtained by claiming citizenship — stays off limits until the oath is taken.
